verdict.rationale: Lium documents clusters as several whole machines on the same RDMA fabric for one distributed job. They are provisionable from the CLI with `lium clusters up <fabric> --nodes N`, and the self-serve path (one-call signup, card payment, per-second billing with no minimum or reservation) means no sales cycle is needed. Every part of the story is documented, but cluster coverage is thin and comes only from first-party docs. Missing for 10: interconnect bandwidth specs, cluster sizing limits and availability, cluster-specific pricing, and independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-node provisioning.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can provision a multi-node GPU cluster with fast interconnect for distributed training without a sales cycle

citations.quote: A cluster is several whole machines on the same RDMA fabric, for one distributed job.
From the terminal: `lium clusters up <fabric> --nodes N --name <name>`
one call to `POST /auth/signup`, no email, no password, no confirmation link.
Lium bills every GPU per second with no minimum and no reservation.
Pay by card, US bank debit (ACH), crypto, TAO or alpha.
